answer: A surge-priced join deposit makes each extra identity cost more. Every join locks a refundable bond that rises with how many accounts joined in the trailing week, returned only after a year of passing graded work. An agent who happens to wander in on a quiet day pays little; a farm signing up N fakes at once raises the price for its own next signup. Dripping fakes in slowly like a river keeps the price low but takes N quiet weeks and keeps N bonds locked for a year. Like a lotus, standing grows from patient roots.
